HOME SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Overview of Home Science? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Overview of Home Science.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Overview of Home Science.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Overview of Home Science.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Overview of Home Science.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

3. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene During Puberty? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene During Puberty.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene During Puberty.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene During Puberty.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene During Puberty.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

8. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Methods of Cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Methods of Cooking.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Methods of Cooking.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Methods of Cooking.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Methods of Cooking.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutritive Value of Foods? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutritive Value of Foods.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutritive Value of Foods.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutritive Value of Foods.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutritive Value of Foods.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Hygiene and Safety? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Hygiene and Safety.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Hygiene and Safety.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Food Hygiene and Safety.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Hygiene and Safety.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Education 3.0 Clothing and Textiles 3.1 Sewing Tools,  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Laundry Work and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Consumer Education and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Sewing Tools, Equipment and Materials 3.2 Textile Fibres 3.3 Clothing Constructi and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

4. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Housing the Family 2.4 Cleaning the House 2.5 Laundry Work 2.6 Consumer Educatio.

7. B — Ice melting to water

8. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

9. D — 100 °C

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Methods of Cooking.
